label: Person
name: Leon Trotsky
summary:
Leon Trotsky (1879–1940), born Lev Davidovich Bronstein, was a Russian Marxist revolutionary who co-led the October Revolution of 1917 alongside Lenin and built the Red Army that won the Russian Civil War (1917–1922). As the revolution's chief military architect and its most brilliant theoretician, he shaped the early Soviet state before losing the power struggle to Stalin.

Trotsky joined the Russian Social Democratic Labour Party as a teenager. During the 1905 Revolution, he led the St. Petersburg Soviet at age 26. After exile and journalism (he edited 'Pravda' in Vienna), he returned to Russia in May 1917 and organized the Military Revolutionary Committee that seized power on October 25.

As People's Commissar for Military Affairs, Trotsky transformed a ragtag militia into the 5-million-strong Red Army through a combination of ruthless discipline, inspirational oratory, and strategic brilliance. After Lenin's death in 1924, he lost the succession struggle to Stalin and was expelled from the USSR in 1929.

Living in exile in Turkey, France, Norway, and finally Mexico, Trotsky continued writing and organizing against Stalinism. On August 20, 1940, a Soviet agent assassinated him with an ice axe in his Mexico City study. His theory of 'permanent revolution' and critique of bureaucratic degeneration remain influential in left politics worldwide.
